Since \(2/7 = 0.\overline{285714}\), \(a_n\) is the integer formed by the first \(n\) digits after the decimal point. Thus \(b_n = a_n - 10a_{n-1}\) is the \(n\)-th decimal digit of \(2/7\).

For \(n=2018\):
\[
2018 \equiv 2 \pmod{6}
\]
The second digit in the repeating block \(285714\) is \(8\).

\[
\boxed{8}
\]
